images.title: Factors of 225 from primes
images.purpose: Show the systematic way to build every factor of 225 by taking its primes one, two, three and four at a time.
images.composition: A row of four prime tiles sits at the top centre; below it a small four row table lists the products, and one final list line sits at the bottom, all with roomy spacing.
exact_structure: Top: exactly 4 prime tiles: two teal #0072B2 tiles 3 and two amber #E69F00 tiles 5, with 225 = 3 × 3 × 5 × 5 to their left.
Table with exactly 4 rows and 2 columns, thin grey #6B7280 lines.
Bottom line: the full list 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 25, 45, 75, 225 with the 1 in reddish purple #CC79A7 to show it is added; exactly 9 numbers in the list.
rejection: the final list with more or fewer than 9 numbers, or any number that is not a factor of 225
the row 2 primes missing 15 or the row 3 primes missing 75
more or fewer than 4 prime tiles
images.takeaway: Combine the primes one, two, three and four at a time, add 1, and you have every factor.
images.description: Prime tiles 3, 3, 5, 5 above a table of products taken one to four at a time, ending in the list of the 9 factors of 225.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on listing all the factors from the primes.
images.teaching_notes: Read the table row by row and notice the 1 is added at the end because it uses no primes.

image_decisions.why: A table of combinations shows the system for listing every factor without missing any.
